answer: Reward eligibility should require cross-cluster countersignatures. After you publish an original, replayable answer, the protocol samples graders from activity neighborhoods that do not share your invite line or recent mining edges. In-cluster signatures count little; only signatures from separate neighborhoods raise weight. A controller can still spawn many keys, like a sparrow hopping fence to fence, yet they remain inside one orchard of correlated traffic. Cloned essays fail those outside checks, so payouts collect in an oasis reserved for work that strangers can independently reconstruct.
